tasks.title: Validate the toolchain sentinel before deleting, and reject pre-SRI installs as unhealthy
tasks.prompt:
You are closing two residual findings from Codex gate round 2 on milestone M0 of the
SXC-1 Trainer project. Repository root: /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1. You own exactly ONE file:

    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh

Do not create or edit any other file. Read /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/briefs/M0-fixes2-triage.md for the full
rationale and the reproduction transcripts; do not re-derive them.

DEPENDENCY-CLOSURE RULE (house rule): every file your verify_commands read must be inside your
own owned_paths, produced by your depends_on closure, or already committed at HEAD.
site/public/ is a build artifact, not committed -- any verify command needing it must run
./scripts/build-site.sh first (committed, idempotent, ~3s). The GHC wasm toolchain is already
installed and healthy at $HOME/.ghc-wasm; no task here requires reinstalling it.

BACKGROUND
This script installs the pinned GHC WebAssembly toolchain (ghc-wasm-meta @
c75985a1b58fb0376eea9149ba5c7b933b3c7455, FLAVOUR=9.14) by cloning the GitHub mirror and running
upstream's setup.sh, whose FIRST destructive action is `rm -rf "$PREFIX"`. A previous round added
validate_prefix() and an SRI-verifying curl shim. Two residuals remain, both reproduced.

=== RESIDUAL 1 (BLOCKER, B1): the sentinel is a NAME check, not a CONTENT check ===
validate_prefix() currently promotes a directory to "recognized toolchain" if a regular file
named .sxc1-toolchain-stamp merely EXISTS, or if an `env` file and a `wasm32-wasi-ghc/`
directory both exist. Content is never validated. All three of these were confirmed to reach the
`rm -rf "$PREFIX"` sink with NO --force, destroying arbitrary user data:
  - a populated directory containing a ZERO-BYTE .sxc1-toolchain-stamp
  - a populated directory containing a MALFORMED (non key=value) stamp
  - a populated directory containing an empty `env` file and an empty `wasm32-wasi-ghc/` dir
The control flow is: validate_prefix promotes on the name -> health_check later REJECTS the
forged marker -> the guard at
    if [ "$FORCE" != "1" ] && health_check 1; then ... exit 0; fi
is therefore false -> control FALLS THROUGH into the destructive install. The guard and the sink
disagree about what counts as "ours", and the fall-through resolves that in favour of deleting.

Fix -- implement validated sentinel + explicit replacement, as three classes:
  CLASS A (validated toolchain): .sxc1-toolchain-stamp exists AND every non-empty line parses as
    key=value AND it carries `ghc_wasm_meta_commit=` whose value is exactly 40 hexadecimal
    characters AND a non-empty `flavour=`. Proceed as today.
    IMPORTANT: do NOT require the stamp to match the CURRENT pin here. A toolchain installed at a
    different pin is still ours and must remain reinstallable -- otherwise pin upgrades break.
  CLASS B (plausible but unvalidated): `env` file AND `wasm32-wasi-ghc/` directory both present,
    but no CLASS A stamp -- e.g. an install interrupted before the stamp was written. REFUSE
    unless --force. With --force, print exactly what will be recursively deleted, then proceed.
    This is the "explicit replacement" property.
  CLASS C (anything else non-empty): refuse ALWAYS. No --force override. A forged marker must
    land here rather than being promoted to CLASS A.
  An absent or empty directory stays acceptable exactly as today.

  SECOND GATE AT THE SINK: because the fall-through above is the actual danger, re-assert the
  classification immediately before invoking upstream setup.sh, and abort if the prefix is not
  (absent | empty | CLASS A | CLASS B-with-force) at that moment. Add a comment saying this is a
  deliberate second gate so a future control-flow edit cannot reach `rm -rf` unvalidated. Keep
  the existing pre-clone validation too -- it is what makes refusals network-free.

=== RESIDUAL 2 (MAJOR, M1): health_check accepts pre-SRI installs ===
health_check parses only ghc_wasm_meta_commit, flavour and ghc_version. It never requires
`sri_verified_downloads`, which only the FIXED installer writes. Confirmed: stripping that key
from the stamp (simulating an install produced by the pre-fix wrapper at the same pin) leaves
`--check` returning 0. The fixed installer therefore no-ops and keeps bindists that were never
SRI-verified -- exactly the upgrade path that matters for anyone who ran M0 before the fix.

Fix: add a constant `EXPECTED_SRI_DOWNLOADS=7` (the pinned setup.sh makes seven `-o` downloads:
wasi-sdk, libffi, Node, binaryen, wasmtime, GHC, cabal). health_check additionally requires the
stamp's `sri_verified_downloads` to parse as an integer >= EXPECTED_SRI_DOWNLOADS. A missing,
non-numeric or too-small value is UNHEALTHY, with a message naming the specific reason so the
user understands a reinstall is about to happen and why.
  Deliberately do NOT introduce a stamp schema-version key: the currently installed toolchain
  already records sri_verified_downloads=7 and must stay healthy, so nobody pays a 17-minute
  reinstall for a metadata-only change. For THIS change the count is the discriminator.
  Also assert at install time that the shim actually verified EXPECTED_SRI_DOWNLOADS downloads,
  and fail the install if it verified fewer -- otherwise the stamp could record a number the
  health check would later accept while downloads were silently skipped.

CONSTRAINTS
- Preserve everything else: --help/--check/--force/--verify-sri-selftest, the pinned constants,
  the pre-clone hard-refuse list (/, $HOME, repo root, ancestors, '..', non-directories), the
  env -u quarantine, the SRI curl shim, the rev-parse pin assertion, `set -euo pipefail`.
- --check must remain a pure, network-free health probe that does not require install-only
  prerequisites (unzip/unzstd/make/cc/disk space).
- Do NOT reinstall the toolchain. Your changes are metadata/validation only and the existing
  install at $HOME/.ghc-wasm must remain healthy after them -- verify that.

DONE LOOKS LIKE
All verify commands below pass. Note the negative-control harness stubs `git` so the real
upstream setup.sh can never land -- it is safe to run at any time and asserts on whether control
REACHES the destructive sink, which is the property that matters. It also contains
false-refusal controls: an empty prefix, a validated CLASS A toolchain under --force, and a
CLASS B directory under --force must all still install.
verify_commands: bash -n /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh && test -x /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh

bash -c 'set -e
W=$(mktemp -d)
cat > "$W/git" <<"EOS"
#!/usr/bin/env bash
if [ "$1" = "clone" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$3"
  printf "#!/usr/bin/env bash\necho \"SETUP_REACHED_PREFIX=\$PREFIX\"\n" > "$3/setup.sh"
  chmod +x "$3/setup.sh"
fi
if [ "$1" = "-C" ] && [ "$3" = "rev-parse" ]; then
  echo c75985a1b58fb0376eea9149ba5c7b933b3c7455
fi
exit 0
EOS
chmod +x "$W/git"
rc=0
reached() { printf "%s" "$1" | grep -q SETUP_REACHED_PREFIX; }

# --- Codex gate-2 scenario + variants: forged markers must NOT reach the rm -rf sink ---
mk() { d="$W/$1"; mkdir -p "$d"; echo IRREPLACEABLE > "$d/precious.txt"; }
mk v1; : > "$W/v1/.sxc1-toolchain-stamp"
mk v2; echo "garbage not key=value" > "$W/v2/.sxc1-toolchain-stamp"
mk v3; mkdir -p "$W/v3/wasm32-wasi-ghc"; : > "$W/v3/env"
mk v4; printf "ghc_wasm_meta_commit=nothex\nflavour=9.14\n" > "$W/v4/.sxc1-toolchain-stamp"
for v in v1 v2 v3 v4; do
  out=$(PATH="$W:$PATH" GHC_WASM_PREFIX="$W/$v" timeout 40 /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh 2>&1 || true)
  if reached "$out"; then echo "FAIL[$v]: forged marker reached setup.sh (rm -rf sink) without --force"; rc=1; fi
  test -f "$W/$v/precious.txt" || { echo "FAIL[$v]: victim data destroyed"; rc=1; }
  out=$(PATH="$W:$PATH" GHC_WASM_PREFIX="$W/$v" timeout 40 /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh --force 2>&1 || true)
  if [ "$v" != "v3" ] && reached "$out"; then echo "FAIL[$v]: --force wiped a non-toolchain directory"; rc=1; fi
done

# --- false-refusal controls: legitimate targets MUST still install ---
mkdir -p "$W/fresh"
out=$(PATH="$W:$PATH" GHC_WASM_PREFIX="$W/fresh" timeout 40 /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh 2>&1 || true)
reached "$out" || { echo "FAIL: refused an empty/new prefix (false refusal)"; rc=1; }
mkdir -p "$W/real/wasm32-wasi-ghc"
printf "ghc_wasm_meta_commit=c75985a1b58fb0376eea9149ba5c7b933b3c7455\nflavour=9.14\nghc_version=9.14.1.20260731\nsri_verified_downloads=7\n" > "$W/real/.sxc1-toolchain-stamp"
out=$(PATH="$W:$PATH" GHC_WASM_PREFIX="$W/real" timeout 40 /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh --force 2>&1 || true)
reached "$out" || { echo "FAIL: --force refused a VALIDATED toolchain (reinstall broken)"; rc=1; }
# class B: plausible-but-unvalidated must refuse plain, allow --force
out=$(PATH="$W:$PATH" GHC_WASM_PREFIX="$W/v3" timeout 40 /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh --force 2>&1 || true)
reached "$out" || { echo "FAIL: --force refused a class-B (env + wasm32-wasi-ghc) directory"; rc=1; }

rm -rf "$W"
test $rc -eq 0 && echo "ok: forged markers refused, legitimate targets still installable"
exit $rc'

bash -c 'set -e; S="$HOME/.ghc-wasm/.sxc1-toolchain-stamp"; B=$(mktemp); cp "$S" "$B"; trap "cp \"$B\" \"$S\"; rm -f \"$B\"" EXIT; grep -v "^sri_verified_downloads=" "$B" > "$S"; if /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh --check >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "FAIL: pre-SRI stamp (no sri_verified_downloads) still accepted as healthy"; exit 1; fi; echo "ok: pre-SRI install is now unhealthy"'

bash -c 'set -e; S="$HOME/.ghc-wasm/.sxc1-toolchain-stamp"; B=$(mktemp); cp "$S" "$B"; trap "cp \"$B\" \"$S\"; rm -f \"$B\"" EXIT; sed "s/^sri_verified_downloads=.*/sri_verified_downloads=3/" "$B" > "$S"; if /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh --check >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "FAIL: too-small sri_verified_downloads accepted"; exit 1; fi; sed "s/^sri_verified_downloads=.*/sri_verified_downloads=notanumber/" "$B" > "$S"; if /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh --check >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "FAIL: non-numeric sri_verified_downloads accepted"; exit 1; fi; echo "ok: count is validated as an integer >= expected"'
/home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh --check
/home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh --verify-sri-selftest

bash -c 'set -e; D=$(mktemp -d); for f in /usr/bin/* /bin/*; do b=$(basename "$f"); case "$b" in unzip|unzstd|make|cc|gcc) continue;; esac; ln -sf "$f" "$D/$b" 2>/dev/null || true; done; PATH="$D" "$D/bash" /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh --check >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "FAIL: --check regressed into needing install-only prerequisites"; exit 1; }; rm -rf "$D"; echo "ok: --check is still a pure health probe"'
grep -q 'EXPECTED_SRI_DOWNLOADS' /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh

bash -c 'set -e; cd /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1; ./scripts/build-site.sh >/dev/null; node -e "const fs=require(\"fs\");const m=new WebAssembly.Module(fs.readFileSync(\"site/public/app.wasm\"));const n=WebAssembly.Module.exports(m).map(e=>e.name);if(!n.includes(\"hs_start\"))process.exit(1);console.log(\"ok: toolchain still builds a valid reactor module\")"'
acceptance_checks: B1: the sentinel is content-validated -- a populated directory with a zero-byte, malformed, or non-hex-commit .sxc1-toolchain-stamp, or with a forged `env` + `wasm32-wasi-ghc/` pair, is REFUSED without --force and its data survives; none of them reach upstream setup.sh.

B1: class B (env + wasm32-wasi-ghc/ present, no valid stamp) refuses without --force but is replaceable WITH --force after printing what will be deleted; class C (any other non-empty directory) refuses always with no --force override.

B1: a second, non-bypassable classification gate runs immediately before setup.sh is invoked, so the health_check fall-through can no longer reach `rm -rf` unvalidated; a comment records why it exists.

B1: no false refusals -- an empty/new prefix installs, and a validated class-A toolchain is still reinstallable with --force (including one pinned at a DIFFERENT commit, so pin upgrades keep working).
M1: health_check requires sri_verified_downloads to be an integer >= EXPECTED_SRI_DOWNLOADS (7); missing, non-numeric and too-small values are all unhealthy with a specific reason in the message.
M1: the install path asserts the shim actually verified EXPECTED_SRI_DOWNLOADS downloads and fails the install if fewer were verified.

The existing $HOME/.ghc-wasm install remains healthy (no reinstall was required), --check stays network-free and free of install-only prerequisites, and every prior control (hard-refuse list, env -u quarantine, SRI shim, pin assertion, --verify-sri-selftest) still passes.

tasks.title: Make the toolchain cache key actually identify the runner image
tasks.prompt:
You are closing one residual finding from Codex gate round 2 on milestone M0 of the
SXC-1 Trainer project. Repository root: /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1. You own exactly ONE file:

    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/.github/workflows/site.yml

Do not create or edit any other file. Read /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/briefs/M0-fixes2-triage.md for rationale.

DEPENDENCY-CLOSURE RULE (house rule): every file your verify_commands read must be inside your
own owned_paths, produced by your depends_on closure, or already committed at HEAD.
site/public/ is a build artifact, not committed -- any verify command needing it must run
./scripts/build-site.sh first (committed, idempotent, ~3s). The GHC wasm toolchain is already
installed and healthy at $HOME/.ghc-wasm; no task here requires reinstalling it.

=== RESIDUAL (MAJOR, M3): the cache key's runner-image segment is empty ===
The toolchain cache key is currently:

    key: ghc-wasm-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ env.ImageOS }}-${{ hashFiles('scripts/install-toolchain.sh') }}

`ImageOS` is a runner-PROCESS environment variable. It is never declared in this workflow's
`env:` keys and never written to $GITHUB_ENV, and GitHub's contexts reference states plainly:

    "The env context contains variables that have been set in a workflow, job, or step.
     It does not contain variables inherited by the runner process."
    https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#env-context

So `${{ env.ImageOS }}` resolves to the EMPTY STRING today and the key is effectively
`ghc-wasm-Linux-X64--<hash>`. The comment above the cache step claims the key "covers OS, arch,
the runner image and the installer script" -- it does not cover the image at all. A same-OS
ubuntu-latest image migration can still restore a native toolchain tree built against different
system libraries. (There are deliberately no restore-keys, so this is the only image guard.)

Fix:
  1. Add a step BEFORE the cache step that composes the identity from the runner's process
     environment and publishes it as a STEP OUTPUT (which the expression context can read):

         - name: Identify runner image
           id: runner-image
           run: echo "id=${ImageOS:-unknown}-${ImageVersion:-unknown}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

     Both ImageOS and ImageVersion are set on GitHub-hosted runners; using both gives a precise
     image identity, and the `:-unknown` defaults make a missing value a VISIBLE literal rather
     than an invisible empty segment. Echo the composed id to the log too, so a cache miss is
     explainable from the run output.
  2. Change the cache key's third segment to `${{ steps.runner-image.outputs.id }}`.
     Remove the `env.ImageOS` reference entirely.
  3. Correct the comment above the cache step: say that the runner image identity comes from a
     step output because the `env` context does not expose runner-process variables, and cite
     the docs URL above so nobody reintroduces `env.ImageOS`.

CONSTRAINTS -- do not disturb anything else in this workflow, all of which is already accepted:
  - workflow-scope `permissions: contents: read`; pages:write/id-token:write ONLY on deploy;
    `persist-credentials: false` on checkout
  - no workflow-level concurrency; per-ref build group cancelling only pull requests; `pages`
    group on deploy alone with cancel-in-progress: false
  - deploy gated on `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' &&
    vars.ENABLE_PAGES == 'true'` (the repo does not exist yet and Pages enablement is still an
    open question with the owner -- this gate must stay safe under any outcome)
  - NO restore-keys on the toolchain cache; installer runs unconditionally; timeout-minutes on
    install/build/verify; the verify step's `result=complete` assertion
  - only first-party actions/*; no Nix/ghcup/stack/node setup steps

DONE LOOKS LIKE
The workflow parses, the structural assertions below pass, and `env.ImageOS` appears nowhere.
You cannot run GitHub Actions locally; in your report, state the shell command you ran to
confirm the composed id is non-empty on a machine that sets ImageOS (or state plainly that this
machine does not set it and that the `:-unknown` default is what you relied on).
verify_commands: python3 -c "import yaml; d=yaml.safe_load(open('/home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/.github/workflows/site.yml')); assert 'build' in d['jobs'] and 'deploy' in d['jobs']; print('workflow parses')"
bash -c '! grep -n "env\.ImageOS" /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/.github/workflows/site.yml || { echo "FAIL: env.ImageOS still referenced (resolves empty)"; exit 1; }; echo "ok: no env.ImageOS"'

python3 - <<'PY'
import yaml
d=yaml.safe_load(open('/home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/.github/workflows/site.yml'))
steps=d['jobs']['build']['steps']
ids=[s.get('id') for s in steps]
tc=[i for i,s in enumerate(steps) if '.ghc-wasm' in str((s.get('with') or {}).get('path',''))]
assert tc, 'no toolchain cache step'
ti=tc[0]
img=[i for i,s in enumerate(steps) if s.get('id')=='runner-image']
assert img, 'no step with id runner-image'
assert img[0] < ti, 'runner-image step must come BEFORE the cache step'
assert 'GITHUB_OUTPUT' in str(steps[img[0]].get('run','')), 'runner-image must publish a step output'
key=str(steps[ti]['with']['key'])
assert 'steps.runner-image.outputs.id' in key, f'cache key does not use the step output: {key}'
assert 'restore-keys' not in (steps[ti].get('with') or {}), 'toolchain cache must have no restore-keys'
assert 'runner.arch' in key and 'install-toolchain.sh' in key, key
print('ok: cache key identifies the runner image via a step output')
PY

python3 - <<'PY'
import yaml
d=yaml.safe_load(open('/home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/.github/workflows/site.yml'))
assert (d.get('permissions') or {}) == {'contents':'read'}, d.get('permissions')
dep=d['jobs']['deploy']
assert (dep.get('permissions') or {}).get('pages')=='write' and (dep.get('permissions') or {}).get('id-token')=='write'
b=d['jobs']['build']
assert 'pages' not in (b.get('permissions') or {})
assert 'concurrency' not in d and b.get('concurrency') and dep.get('concurrency',{}).get('group')=='pages'
assert 'ENABLE_PAGES' in str(dep.get('if',''))
steps=b['steps']
co=[s for s in steps if 'checkout' in str(s.get('uses',''))][0]
assert (co.get('with') or {}).get('persist-credentials') in (False,'false')
ver=[s for s in steps if 'check-site.sh' in str(s.get('run',''))][0]
assert ver.get('timeout-minutes') and 'result=complete' in str(ver['run'])
inst=[s for s in steps if 'install-toolchain.sh' in str(s.get('run',''))][0]
assert 'if' not in inst
print('ok: all previously-accepted CI hardening intact')
PY

bash -c 'set -e; cd /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1; for s in scripts/install-toolchain.sh scripts/build-site.sh scripts/check-site.sh; do grep -q "$s" .github/workflows/site.yml || { echo "workflow does not call $s"; exit 1; }; git ls-files -s "$s" | grep -q "^100755" || { echo "$s not committed as executable"; exit 1; }; done; echo "ok: referenced scripts committed and executable"'

bash -c 'ImageOS=ubuntu24 ImageVersion=20260801.1 bash -c "echo id=\${ImageOS:-unknown}-\${ImageVersion:-unknown}" | grep -q "id=ubuntu24-20260801.1" && bash -c "echo id=\${ImageOS:-unknown}-\${ImageVersion:-unknown}" | grep -q "id=unknown-unknown" && echo "ok: identity expression behaves with and without the runner vars"'
acceptance_checks: M3: `env.ImageOS` appears nowhere in the workflow; a step with id `runner-image`, ordered before the cache step, composes ${ImageOS:-unknown}-${ImageVersion:-unknown} into $GITHUB_OUTPUT and logs it.

M3: the toolchain cache key's image segment is ${{ steps.runner-image.outputs.id }}, so a runner-image migration changes the key; a missing runner variable yields a visible `unknown` literal rather than an invisible empty segment.
M3: the comment above the cache step explains that the identity comes from a step output because the env context does not expose runner-process variables, and cites GitHub's contexts documentation.
The toolchain cache still has no restore-keys and the key still includes runner.os, runner.arch and hashFiles('scripts/install-toolchain.sh').

Every previously-accepted CI property is intact: contents:read at workflow scope, pages/id-token on deploy only, persist-credentials:false, per-ref build concurrency with the pages group on deploy alone, the vars.ENABLE_PAGES deploy gate, unconditional installer, timeout-minutes, and the result=complete assertion.
Only first-party actions/* are used and every referenced script exists and is executable.

tasks.title: Clean up the sub-path bundle copy on every exit path and preserve WebSocket error causes
tasks.prompt:
You are closing the two new findings from Codex gate round 2 on milestone M0 of the
SXC-1 Trainer project. Repository root: /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1. You own exactly these two files:

    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/check-site.sh
    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/browser-check.mjs

Do not create or edit any other file. Read /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/briefs/M0-fixes2-triage.md for rationale.

DEPENDENCY-CLOSURE RULE (house rule): every file your verify_commands read must be inside your
own owned_paths, produced by your depends_on closure, or already committed at HEAD.
site/public/ is a build artifact, not committed -- any verify command needing it must run
./scripts/build-site.sh first (committed, idempotent, ~3s). The GHC wasm toolchain is already
installed and healthy at $HOME/.ghc-wasm; no task here requires reinstalling it.

=== NEW1 (MINOR): the sub-path bundle temp directory leaks on any non-happy exit ===
check-site.sh's cleanup() trap tracks SERVER_PIDS and SERVER_LOGS only. The GitHub-Pages
sub-path deployability test creates SUBPATH_TMP with `mktemp -d` (around line 599) and removes
it only on the happy path (around line 604), after the second browser stage returns. A SIGINT or
SIGTERM during either browser stage -- or any `set -e` failure between the mktemp and the
explicit rm -- leaves a full copy of the built bundle behind. Reproduced: interrupting a run
1.2 seconds in leaked a 2.9 MB /tmp/sxc1-check-site-subpath.* directory. This is larger than the
server-log leak fixed in the previous round, and it was introduced by that round's M9 fix.

Fix:
  1. Add a TEMP_DIRS array beside SERVER_PIDS/SERVER_LOGS, initialised before the traps are
     installed so cleanup can never reference it unset.
  2. Register SUBPATH_TMP on the line immediately after `mktemp -d` -- not later, or the window
     the finding describes simply moves.
  3. Remove every registered directory in cleanup(), which already runs on EXIT, INT and TERM.
  4. Keep the explicit happy-path `rm -rf` if you like, but UNREGISTER the entry there so
     cleanup cannot later remove a path that has been reused by another process.
  5. If any other `mktemp -d` exists or is added in this script, register it the same way.

=== NEW2 (NIT): WebSocket error diagnostics discard the underlying cause ===
browser-check.mjs's fatal WebSocket error listener (around lines 624-625) falls back from
`ev.message` to interpolating the event, so a transport failure commonly reports
`CDP WebSocket error: [object ErrorEvent]`, hiding whether Chrome reset the socket, refused a
frame, or something else. Settlement is correct -- this is purely diagnostic quality, on a path
that now matters because the deadline work made it reachable.

Fix: prefer, in order, `ev.error?.stack`, then `ev.error?.message`, then `ev.message`, then
`String(ev)`. Node's WebSocket ErrorEvent exposes the underlying cause on `ev.error`. Apply the
same ordering to any sibling `close`/`error` handler that formats an event for a message.

CONSTRAINTS
- These are the only two changes. Do not restructure either script, do not rename checks, and do
  not alter any assertion semantics -- both files are otherwise accepted by review.
- check-site.sh must still: perform no build; keep --help/--skip-browser/--port/--dir; print
  per-check `ok - `/`FAIL - ` lines; run every check then summarise; emit `result=complete` vs
  `result=structural-only`; bind servers to 127.0.0.1 only; and keep the server-log cleanup and
  server-identity verification added previously.
- browser-check.mjs must keep zero npm dependencies, its exit-code contract (0 pass, 1 assertion
  failure, 2 harness error), its deadline bounding, and its --self-test.

DONE LOOKS LIKE
`./scripts/check-site.sh` still reports 20/20 and `result=complete`; interrupting a run mid-flight
leaves no /tmp/sxc1-check-site-subpath.* directory; and `node scripts/browser-check.mjs
